title: All-short attention: kill the long (2048) layers
description: WINDOW_PATTERN "SSSL" -> "SSSS" and deleted the window_sizes[-1] = (long_window, 0) line, so all 8 layers use window 512 instead of 6x512 + 2x2048.
reflection: Clear, large NEGATIVE: val_bpb 0.996919 vs the //4 baseline's 0.989668 (n=2, 0.989668/0.989981), i.e. +0.00725 at ~12 sd. Tokens were essentially MATCHED (488.6M vs 486.5M), so the entire delta is quality, not throughput. Two findings. (1) Global attention layers are load-bearing and the -0.002 quality residual from 1024->512 was NOT 'less attention is better' - it was 'local layers can be narrower while the two full-2048 layers remain'. My cross-document-contamination mechanism predicted the opposite sign for the global layers and is falsified for them. (2) Shaving attention FLOPs buys almost nothing here: -8.5% FLOPs/token (220.4M -> 201.3M) returned only +0.4% tokens because MFU fell 35.89% -> 32.96%. Uniform short windows are LESS efficient per FLOP than a mixed pattern. The window axis should be considered closed in the shrinking direction; if anything the interesting probe is now MORE global attention (e.g. 'SSLL' or a third long layer), not less.
